title: Rigidification independence over complete strictly local regular rings
statement: Fix the quotient-resolution construction of [lem-per-rigidified-quotient-tower-comparison], using the saturated fan rule induced by one normalized characteristic-zero desingularization algorithm functorial for regular morphisms, as in [lem-per-characteristic-zero-log-resolution-independence]. Let $X=\coprod_{i=1}^m\operatorname{Spec}A_i$, where $m$ is finite and each $A_i$ is a complete Noetherian regular local ring with separably closed residue field [def-weil-regular-scheme], [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. Let a finite group $G$ act tamely on $X$, with abelian geometric inertia and freely outside a $G$-strict strict normal crossings boundary $B$ [def-trf-strict-normal-crossings-boundary]. Let $\overline B$ and $\overline B'$ be two invariant normal crossings boundaries containing $B$ such that each enlarged divisorial log structure is very tame [def-trf-fs-log-blowup]. Resolve the log quotients for these two rigidifications by the fixed rule, pull back in fs log schemes, and retain the underlying normalized blowup towers with ordered centers. The two resulting towers on $X$ are equal, including the order and the defining ideal sheaves of all centers. The equality also holds for a finite disjoint union with permuted components; it is not merely equality of contracted towers on each separate component.

source.place: VIII Lemma 5.5.2 and proof, printed pp.127--128; characteristic-zero independence used there is Theorem 3.4.15, printed pp.113--114.

proof.text: Choose the common ambient diagram $X\xleftarrow{h}U\xrightarrow{j}Y$ and $E\subset E_1,E_2$ from [lem-per-simultaneous-cohen-rigidification-lift]. Its hypotheses are exactly the complete-local, tame abelian-inertia and two very-tame rigidification hypotheses here. In particular both maps are strict and inert for each rigidification, and $h$ is a surjective finite union of component isomorphisms. On the single underlying quotient $Q=Y/G$, the two fs log regular structures have characteristic-zero generic points on every log stratum. This diagram is constructed for the entire finite disjoint union, with its permuted components.

source.place: VIII 5.5.2, pp.127--128: simultaneous ambient lift and disjoint-union paragraph.

proof.text: Apply [lem-per-characteristic-zero-log-resolution-independence] on $Q$ with the identity scheme isomorphism and the two quotient log structures. Use precisely the algorithm inducing our fixed fan rule. This gives equal underlying normalized quotient-resolution towers, with the same ordered center ideals, on the whole $Q$. The ambient lemma supplies fs log regularity and characteristic-zero generic stratum points; the independence theorem requires no finite-type hypothesis on $Q$.

source.place: VIII 3.4.15 and the last two paragraphs of 5.5.2, pp.113--114,128.

proof.text: Pull back the two quotient log towers to $Y$. By the universal property in [def-trf-fs-log-blowup], fs base change of a log blowup is the log blowup of the pulled-back log ideal: maps from any fs test object on either side are exactly maps making that ideal invertible. Apply [lem-trf-log-blowup-normalization] at each stage and on each integral component. The common ambient lemma supplies integral affine components initially; blowing up a nonzero ideal and normalizing in its function field keeps each component integral. For a quotient-stage log ideal $\mathcal I_r$, put $J_r=\alpha(\mathcal I_r)\mathcal O_{Q_r}$. The ring ideal generated by its pullback on $Y_r$ is exactly $J_r\mathcal O_{Y_r}$, by compatibility of log structure maps. Thus the next underlying stage is the normalized blowup of this extended ideal. Step 2 identifies $Q_r$ and $J_r$ for both towers. Starting from the same map $Y\to Q$, induction therefore identifies $Y_r$, its map to $Q_r$, and its next center for both towers. This gives equality of the full ordered centered towers on $Y$, even though their log structures differ. The argument is simultaneous on all components; it never contracts a tower on an individual component.

Apply strict inert tower comparison [lem-per-rigidified-quotient-tower-comparison] to $j$ for each lifted boundary; its fixed rule is the smooth-functorial fan rule $\mathcal R_{\mathcal F}$ of [lem-per-characteristic-zero-log-resolution-independence]. The same centered tower on $Y$ has the same contracted pullback to $U$, since its pulled-back ideals and hence deleted unit-center stages agree. This proves equality of the two towers constructed on $U$. Apply comparison also to $h:U\to X$. No stage of either tower on $X$ is a unit-center stage. Indeed, the quotient tower on $X/G$ is $T_{\mathcal F}$, all of whose centers have nonempty zero locus [lem-per-characteristic-zero-log-resolution-independence], and each stage map $X_r\to(X/G)_r$ is surjective: $X\to X/G$ is integral, normalized blowups are universally closed, so inductively $X_r\to(X/G)_r$ is universally closed, and its image contains the dense complement of the exceptional locus. As $h$ is surjective and $U_r=X_r\times_XU$, the inverse image of each center in $U_r$ remains nonempty. Thus the uncontracted pullbacks to $U$ agree with their full ordered center ideals. On each component of $X$, at every stage choose any copy in $U$ mapping isomorphically to that component; equality of the pulled-back ideals there is equality of the original ideals. Induction on the synchronized stages gives the required equality on $X$. When $X$ is empty both towers are empty. This argument keeps one common indexing for all permuted components.

proof_origin.place: VIII Lemma 5.5.2 with Corollary 5.4.4 and Theorem 3.4.15, pp.113--114,127--128. The split-copy cover spells out the inertia induction and the equality of center ideals.
